original_problem.title: B
original_problem.description:
Treeland is a country in which there are n towns connected by n - 1 two-way road such that it's possible to get from any town to any other town. 

In Treeland there are 2k universities which are located in different towns. 

Recently, the president signed the decree to connect universities by high-speed network.The Ministry of Education understood the decree in its own way and decided that it was enough to connect each university with another one by using a cable. Formally, the decree will be done! 

To have the maximum sum in the budget, the Ministry decided to divide universities into pairs so that the total length of the required cable will be maximum. In other words, the total distance between universities in k pairs should be as large as possible. 

Help the Ministry to find the maximum total distance. Of course, each university should be present in only one pair. Consider that all roads have the same length which is equal to 1. 


-----Input-----

The first line of the input contains two integers n and k (2 ≤ n ≤ 200 000, 1 ≤ k ≤ n / 2) — the number of towns in Treeland and the number of university pairs. Consider that towns are numbered from 1 to n. 

The second line contains 2k distinct integers u_1, u_2, ..., u_2k (1 ≤ u_{i} ≤ n) — indices of towns in which universities are located. 

The next n - 1 line contains the description of roads. Each line contains the pair of integers x_{j} and y_{j} (1 ≤ x_{j}, y_{j} ≤ n), which means that the j-th road connects towns x_{j} and y_{j}. All of them are two-way roads. You can move from any town to any other using only these roads. 


-----Output-----

Print the maximum possible sum of distances in the division of universities into k pairs.


-----Examples-----
Input
7 2
1 5 6 2
1 3
3 2
4 5
3 7
4 3
4 6

Output
6

Input
9 3
3 2 1 6 5 9
8 9
3 2
2 7
3 4
7 6
4 5
2 1
2 8

Output
9



-----Note-----

The figure below shows one of possible division into pairs in the first test. If you connect universities number 1 and 6 (marked in red) and universities number 2 and 5 (marked in blue) by using the cable, the total distance will equal 6 which will be the maximum sum in this example. 

 [Image]

difference_plan.rationale: Objective changed from computing a scalar maximum value to counting the number of configurations achieving it. Core constraints now explicitly encode the equivalence rule and the edge-flow condition that characterizes maximizers. The invariant shifts from an upper bound to a lock on edge flows, tying maximization to a fixed flow pattern.
difference_plan.summary: We count the distinct pairings that achieve the maximum total distance, redefining the output type, adding deduplication rules, and reconstructing the state space for counting.

components.role_description: Two integers: number of stops and number of gate pairs
List of distinct stop indices where gates are located
Undirected edges defining the bus network (tree)

constraints.name: complete_pairing
constraints.description: The 2k gates must be partitioned into exactly k disjoint unordered pairs, with each gate belonging to exactly one pair.

constraints.name: distinct_nodes_for_gates
constraints.description: All 2k gates are located at mutually distinct stops (i.e., no two gates share the same stop).

constraints.name: unit_edge_weight
constraints.description: Every road segment has the same length equal to 1, so the distance between two gates is the number of edges on the unique tree path.

constraints.name: max_distance_condition
constraints.description: A pairing achieves the maximum total distance if and only if for every edge, the number of paired paths passing through that edge is exactly the smaller of the numbers of gates in the two connected components after removing that edge.

constraints.name: equivalence_rule
constraints.description: Two pairings are considered the same if they consist of exactly the same set of k unordered pairs of gate stops. The order of pairs or the order within a pair is irrelevant.

objective.description: Count the number of distinct pairings (as defined by the equivalence rule) that satisfy the maximum-distance condition, modulo 1000000007.

invariants.name: edge_flow_upper_bound_lock
invariants.description: For any pairing that satisfies the max-distance condition, the flow on each edge is fixed to the smaller gate count of the two sides. Conversely, any pairing achieving this fixed flow on all edges automatically attains the maximum total distance, which is the sum of these smaller counts.

invariants.name: fixed_total_distance
invariants.description: The maximum total distance is uniquely determined by the tree and gate placements, equal to sum over edges of min(cnt_left, cnt_right).

generated_problem.title: 公交闸机最优配对方案计数
generated_problem.description:
城市公交网络包含 n 个站点和 n−1 条双向道路，任意两站点可以相互到达，形成树形结构。
为了方便通勤统计，公交公司在其中 2k 个站点安装了闸机，每站至多安装一个闸机，所有闸机所在站点互不相同。
每位通勤者会从一个闸机刷卡进站，从另一个闸机刷卡出站，其所乘车辆经过的道路总长度即为本次通勤的距离（每条道路长度均为 1）。
现在，公司希望刚好把这 2k 个闸机两两配对，形成 k 对进出站组合（每对中的两个闸机没有顺序，且不同对之间也不考虑顺序），使得所有 k 对通勤的距离之和达到最大。

可以证明，一个配对方案的总距离达到最大的充要条件是：对于任意一条道路，设将该道路断开后，两侧的闸机数量分别为 a 和 b（不妨设 a≤b），则该方案中恰好有 a 个配对中的路径经过了这条道路。

请计算有多少种不同的闸机配对方案能够使总通勤距离达到最大。由于答案可能很大，请输出方案数对 1,000,000,007 取模的结果。
generated_problem.input_format:
第一行包含两个整数 n 和 k，分别表示站点总数和需要形成的通勤对数。
第二行包含 2k 个互不相同的整数，表示安装有闸机的站点编号。
接下来 n−1 行，每行包含两个整数 u 和 v，表示一条连接站点 u 和站点 v 的双向道路。

输入保证所有道路构成一棵树，且 1≤k≤n/2，2≤n≤200,000。
generated_problem.output_format: 一个整数，表示达到最大总距离的不同配对方案数对 1,000,000,007 取模的结果。
constraints: 所有闸机所在站点编号均为 1..n 且互不相同

samples.explanation: 唯一的方案是将闸机 1 与 5 配对、闸机 2 与 4 配对。此时各条边上的经过次数分别为：1−2:1，2−3:2，3−4:2，4−5:1，均达到上限，总距离 6 为最大。没有其他方案。

共有 3 种方案：
• (1,2) 和 (3,4)
• (1,3) 和 (2,4)
• (1,4) 和 (2,3)
每种方案中，边 1−2 被经过 1 次，边 2−3 被经过 1 次，边 2−4 被经过 1 次，均达到上限，总距离 3 为最大。

generated_problem.notes:
两个配对方案视为相同当且仅当它们所包含的无序闸机对的集合完全一致。
输出结果对 1,000,000,007 取模。
题目保证至少存在一种最优方案。

difference_plan.summary: We count the distinct pairings that achieve the maximum total distance, redefining the output type, adding deduplication rules, and reconstructing the state space for counting.

applied_helpers.selection_reason: Fulfills rule requirement to explicitly define counting objects and deduplication.
schema_changes: Added equivalence_rule constraint to define what constitutes distinct pairings.
Objective redefined to count distinct pairings modulo prime.
Invariant extended to justify that the max-distance condition fixes edge flows, making counting well-defined.
applied_helpers.innovation_reason: Turns the answer from a numeric optimum into a combinatorial enumeration, requiring explicit object definition.
applied_helpers.difficulty_reason: Forces solver to handle deduplication in counting, which increases combinatorial complexity.

applied_helpers.selection_reason: Required to decompose the solution space into DP units for counting.
schema_changes: Core constraints no longer rely on a global optimality condition; instead they enforce an edge-flow condition that decomposes naturally along tree edges.
Invariant now explicitly ties the flow condition to a fixed per-edge value, enabling DP on subtrees.
applied_helpers.innovation_reason: Shifts problem structure from a single global sum to a local per-edge invariant, enabling counting via subtree decomposition.
applied_helpers.difficulty_reason: Solver must design a DP state that tracks unpaired gates per subtree and combine correctly, significantly harder than computing a single max.

applied_helpers.selection_reason: Ensures the main solve objective is counting, not a side note.
schema_changes: Objective explicitly demands counting as the primary output.
Core constraints now include the max-distance condition as part of the eligibility for counting, so the solver must enforce it to count correctly.
applied_helpers.innovation_reason: Makes counting the central algorithmic challenge, not merely attaching a modulo to the max value.
applied_helpers.difficulty_reason: The problem now requires the solver to integrate optimality verification directly into the counting process, preventing simplistic bypasses.

algorithmic_delta_claim.seed_solver_core: DFS to count gates in each subtree, then accumulate min(cnt_left, cnt_right) to get maximum distance.
algorithmic_delta_claim.reusable_subroutines: Subtree gate counting (same DFS as seed) can be reused as a preprocessing step to compute the fixed flow on each edge.
algorithmic_delta_claim.new_solver_core: Tree DP with state (u, i) counting ways to pair i gates in the subtree with external gates while satisfying edge-flow constraints. The DP merges children and processes the node's own gate.
algorithmic_delta_claim.new_proof_obligation: Prove that the DP recurrence correctly counts each distinct pairing exactly once under the equivalence rule, and that the edge-flow condition is both necessary and sufficient for maximum distance, thereby ensuring the counting objective is well-defined.
algorithmic_delta_claim.why_direct_reuse_fails: The seed problem only evaluates a single maximum integer. Directly outputting the number of pairings from the seed solution is impossible because the optimal solution does not enumerate or count them. Counting requires a fundamentally different algorithmic structure.

review_context.anti_shallow_rationale: This problem is not a shallow relabeling; it changes the core output type from a scalar to a count with modulo, introduces a nontrivial equivalence rule for pairings, replaces the simple edge accumulation with a DP over tree decompositions, and adds proof obligations around uniqueness and sufficiency of the flow condition. The state factorization into subtree DP units with internal/external pairing distinction constitutes a substantial restructuring.
